valley.drawingAlt: A wide meadow above a still sea. A small seed lies in the grass.
locals: Here nobody runs out of berries, so nobody counts them.
A gift here costs nothing. We give all day, and it means very little.
Wisp sits apart from us and looks at the ridge.

notes.title: Costly signals
notes.science: A gift that costs the giver something says more than a free one.
notes.limits: Here a gift warms a friend only a fifth as much as in Kith. A keepsake from you always warms by the same large amount.
notes.counter: A small free kindness, given often, can still mean a lot.
notes.question: What did you give up to show you cared?

sources.label: Mate Selection: A Selection for a Handicap, Zahavi, 1975
Signaling Theory, Strategic Interaction, and Symbolic Capital, Bliege Bird and Smith, 2005

notes.title: Wisp can choose
notes.science: Wisp comes home only if Wisp is warm toward you and Kith is warm too.
notes.limits: Wisp weighs only those two numbers, once, at a dusk.
notes.counter: Some friends come back for reasons no one can see.
notes.question: Was Kith a place worth coming back to?

sources.label: Place Attachment: How Far Have We Come in the Last 40 Years?, Lewicka, 2011
